title: Active Variable
description: Schema for an Active Variable (AV) — a project-scope (or user_local) variable that instances reference via 'ref:'. Per OBJECT-MODEL.md §13. AVs are NOT definitions (no reusable physical truth) and NOT instances (don't fill a definition's parameters); they are a separate kind that holds a typed value the cross-FK validator resolves through when an instance parameter uses 'ref:' instead of 'value:'.

kind.description: AVs validate against this schema only — kind must be exactly 'active_variable'.

origin.description: AVs live in projects (one-project scope) or user_local (cross-project personal defaults). Never builtin or community. Per OBJECT-MODEL.md §13.

layer.description: AVs cross layers — they configure devices, materials, behaviors, anything. Per OBJECT-MODEL.md §4 cross_layer designation.

parameter_type.description: What type of value this AV holds. Matches the consuming parameter's 'type' field on definitions. Cross-FK validator checks that the AV's parameter_type matches the consuming parameter's type.

value.description: The actual value of this AV. For quantity AVs: a quantity value (scalar, range, condition_bound, equation, curve, lookup_table, or unknown_user_supplied at project/user_local). For ref-type AVs (material_ref / shape_ref / object_ref): a bare string id pointing at a definition. For enum AVs: a bare string. For bool AVs: a boolean. For numeric AVs: a number.

provenance.description: Optional. Project-origin AVs can be user-set without provenance per the anti-placeholder rules (unknown_user_supplied is permitted at project/user_local). When provenance is supplied (e.g., a user cites IPC J-STD-020 for their default reflow temperature), it follows the same fragment shape used elsewhere.
